This data element represents the date when the victimization related to intimate partner violence (IPV) was first documented in the records of the agency providing data to the IPV surveillance system. 6. If IPV documentation arises from routine screening or other forms of disclosure, there may not be a specific violent episode associated with the date of documentation. 7. The Date of agency documentation of the most recent violent episode is recorded as a timestamp with a field length of 26 characters. 8. This data can be used to calculate the victim's age and to differentiate between victims with the same name. 11. If the date of birth is unknown, the year can be estimated based on the victim's age. 12. The Race of Victim field describes or defines the victim's race. 13. Data on race is utilized in public health surveillance, as well as in epidemiologic, clinical, and health services research. 14. For over 20 years, the Federal government has promoted the use of standardized language to ensure uniformity and comparability of data on race and ethnicity for population groups. 15. The development of these data standards was largely driven by new responsibilities to enforce civil rights laws. 16. Data was required to monitor equal access in areas such as housing, education, employment, and other domains for populations historically subjected to discrimination and differential treatment based on race or ethnicity. 17. Examples of such applications include school registration and mortgage lending applications, as well as medical and other research. 18. The racial categories represent a socio-political construct designed to collect data on the race and ethnicity of broad population groups in the United States. 19. Race is a concept used to differentiate population groups primarily based on physical characteristics inherited through descent. 20. Racial categories are neither precise nor mutually exclusive, and the concept of race lacks a clear scientific definition. 21. In the United States, the common use of race draws upon differences not only in physical attributes but also in ancestry and geographic origins. 22. Since 1977, the Federal government has sought to standardize data on race and ethnicity across its agencies. 23. The 1997 directive was developed to meet Federal legislative and program requirements, and these standards are widely used in both public and private sectors. 24. The directive provides five basic racial categories but states that the collection of race data need not be limited to these categories. 25. However, any additional reporting that includes more detailed categories must be organized in a way that allows aggregation into the five basic groups. 26. Although the directive does not specify a method for determining an individual's race, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) prefers self-identification over observer identification whenever possible. 27. The directive specifies that individuals of mixed racial origins should be coded using multiple categories rather than a single multiracial category. 28. The Race of Victim data type is a coded element with a field length of 60 characters. 29. If the agency providing data to the IPV surveillance system uses multiple racial categories, the system also allows for multiple racial categories to be coded. 30. Data on ethnicity is used in public health surveillance, as well as in epidemiologic, clinical, and health services research. 31. Ethnicity is a concept used to differentiate population groups based on shared cultural characteristics or geographic origins.
